issues.description: RevokeErr exposed to API without sanitization, capability gate, or documented redaction contract
issues.detail: All six reviewers flagged this. The PR author explicitly asks whether it's safe to surface RevokeErr; the answer is shipped without resolution. Backend error strings routinely contain paths, URLs, driver messages, and credential fragments. Either redact/truncate at the write site, gate the field behind a sudo/root capability, or state and enforce an invariant that revoke errors never carry sensitive content.

issues.description: Rename FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo breaks exported API and broadens contract without restating it
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported ExpirationManager method; renaming churns downstream callers for cosmetic gain. The new name promises generic 'info' but the postcondition remains a partially-populated leaseEntry with an implicit allowlist. Either keep the old name as a deprecated alias, or introduce an explicit LeaseInfo struct and document exactly which fields are populated.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport redaction property is enumerated, not structurally enforced
issues.detail: The function hand-copies fields from leaseEntry with no mechanism to force a decision when leaseEntry grows a new sensitive field. Returning *leaseEntry conflates the authoritative record with the export view. Introduce a distinct ExportedLeaseInfo/LeaseView struct so the type itself is the contract, and add a test that fails when new leaseEntry fields appear.

issues.description: Metric label 'fetch-lease-times' is now stale after the function rename
issues.detail: metrics.MeasureSince still emits 'expire.fetch-lease-times' and TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable keeps its old name. Either rename the metric and test deliberately (and call it out as a telemetry change), or keep the metric name and add a comment so future maintainers don't silently 'fix' it. Silent mismatch confuses ops later.

issues.description: Test coverage only asserts path; namespace_path and revoke_error branches are untested
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases checks resp.Data['path'] but exercises neither the conditional emission of namespace_path (nil/empty namespace) nor revoke_error (empty vs populated). Add cases for a lease in a child namespace, a forced revoke failure, and assertions that sensitive fields (ClientToken, Secret.InternalData, Auth) are absent from the response.

issues.description: OpenAPI schema marks path as Required but le.Path may be empty for some lease shapes
issues.detail: The framework path spec declares path Required:true while namespace_path and revoke_error are optional. Token leases or irrevocable entries loaded from storage may have empty Path. Either enforce a precondition that every lease reaching handleLeaseLookup has a non-empty Path, or drop Required:true so the schema does not lie to generated clients.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a small, well-shaped patch with one load-bearing security gap and one gratuitous API break. RevokeErr is surfaced to API consumers without sanitization, capability gating, or a stated redaction invariant — the PR author flagged this explicitly and shipped it anyway. The FetchLeaseTimes rename breaks an exported method without an alias and silently broadens the contract while leaving the metric label, an old test name, and the projection type unchanged. Test coverage exercises only the path field, leaving the two conditional new fields and the absence-of-leakage property untested. Ship-blocking until RevokeErr exposure is decided structurally and the rename is either reverted/aliased or accompanied by an explicit ExportedLeaseInfo type.
